items.title: 61539_Butter Jackson oral history interview
items.q: Willie was tight in there and, of course, Tizol knew the band anyway.

ctx.x: And we -- the people -- when Duke let us play what we wanted to play, and we didn't do nothing but swing all night long. That band was fantastic. And the band had tightened up just like that by the time we got back to New York and played

the one-nighters. Willie was tight in there and, of course, Tizol knew the band anyway. And Louie Bellson was cooking, he was cooking. He had taken a lot of the arrangements that he didn't know or he figured he didn't know, he would take a first trumpet part, the first trombone part, and the first saxophone part and take that music home and make a drum part so he could play it right, and he did play it right.

Here is another short called 'Caravan,' three minutes long. It was probably one of those -- yeah, made by Snyder. They made them for those visual jukeboxes, a little film that would go on when you put your money in, and apparently, they did 'Caravan.' It says 'Duke Ellington and his orchestra played the title number with solo by Juan Tizol, trombone, and featuring Jimmy Hamilton, Willie Smith, Russell Procope, Paul Gonzalves, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Willie Cook, Cat Anderson, Britt Woodman, Quentin Jackson, and…
